ashley: spotting a burst of pending tiny-gang pods in us-west2-rack5. Lots of 0.5/1 GPU leftovers, nodes in rack5 entering soft-evict cycles. NIC p95 spiked to ~210ms at 15:02 UTC. :confused:

matt: can you paste `kubectl describe pod`/node for one pending pod? want to see taints/score reasons.

ashley: snippet:
`Warning FailedScheduling 0/120 nodes available: 38 had taints, 82 insufficient GPUs`
`Node warmpool-5-07: Taints: gpu/warmpool:NoSchedule, Network p95=212ms p50=40ms`

leo: same pattern as last month. Scheduler penalizes high-interconnect nodes and spreads, which increases fragmentation.

sarah: quick options: 1) run descheduler dry-run to see compact candidates, 2) temporarily lower topologySpread weight for tiny-gang canary, 3) untaint a couple warmpool nodes in rack5 as compact targets.

jordan: +1 descheduler dry-run first. Evicting during a latency spike could make tail latency worse. cap evictions if we proceed.

ashley: running descheduler dry-run now. will only untaint if dry-run suggests safe compaction.

sre-bot: incident INF-6021 opened: "us-west2 rack5 NIC p95 oscillation -> scheduler spread" assigned to eng-platform. Priority=P3.

ashley: dry-run output: `candidates=51, would compact into 13 nodes, recommended evict=28 low-priority tiny-gang pods`

matt: ok runbook: 1) patch test tiny-gang to preferred anti-affinity, 2) untaint warmpool-5-03/5-04 for 10m, 3) run descheduler with `--eviction-rate=10m` and monitor evictions and GPU_fragmentation metric. rollback if evictions>150 in 10m or job latency SLO breach.

ashley: applying canary changes to rack5 only. monitoring now. will report back in 15m. :thumbsup:
